Post-Soviet Birthplaces in Sarasota County

PLACE OF BIRTH · SARASOTA COUNTY, FLORIDA

A local look at birthplace estimates for the former Soviet republics.

“Sarasota Bay” by Ryan Hodnett, CC BY-SA 4.0.

“Post-Soviet” describes a shared historical context, not one ethnicity, language, or migration story. The Census Bureau’s American Community Survey reports birthplace for foreign-born residents, not ancestry or identity. This dashboard is one small window into Sarasota County’s communities; it cannot tell us why anyone moved or how they identify.

Birthplace estimates over time

Choose up to three republics in the list, or use the legend. Azerbaijan and Georgia have separate estimates starting in 2022; Estonia, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan are not separately reported. Unavailable countries remain listed but disabled. Missing estimates are never treated as zero. Neighboring ACS five-year periods overlap.

Showing 3 of 3 allowed selections.

Regional comparison

Regions are project-defined groupings, not Census categories. The chart adds only countries with separate birthplace estimates in each period; coverage in the hover text makes partial totals visible. Older estimates therefore may cover fewer countries than newer ones.

Project-defined region Included republics
Eastern Europe Belarus, Moldova, Russia, Ukraine
Central Asia Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan
Caucasus Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia
Baltics Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania

Regional margins of error are approximate combinations of the reported country margins; see About for details.

Estimated population change

The chart compares each country’s earliest and latest available estimate. Bars show estimated change; whiskers show an approximate margin of error for the difference. Changes within or near the whiskers are especially uncertain. Even changes outside them are not definitive significance tests because ACS five-year periods overlap.
